import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import numpy as np

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Create a scatter plot to visualize the relationship between megapixels and price,
# with sensor type as a distinguishing factor (hue and style).
# A log scale for price is often useful for financial data due to wide ranges.
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 7))
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='megapixels',
    y='price_usd',
    hue='sensor_type',
    style='sensor_type', # Use style to differentiate for colorblindness and clarity
    s=100,               # Adjust marker size
    alpha=0.7            # Add some transparency
)

# Apply a logarithmic scale to the y-axis (price) for better visualization of skewed data
plt.yscale('log')

# Add title and labels for clarity
plt.title('Camera Price vs. Megapixels by Sensor Type', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Price (USD, Log Scale)', fontsize=12)

# Improve legend placement to avoid overlapping with data points
plt.legend(title='Sensor Type', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left', frameon=True)

# Add a grid for easier reading of values, especially with log scale
plt.grid(True, which="both", ls="--", c='0.7', alpha=0.7)

# Adjust layout to make room for the legend outside the plot area
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.85, 1])

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
